title: League of Legends Patch 26.15 Notes
overview: Patch 26.15 kicks off Ranked Season 3 with a ground-up Bel'Veth rework, nerfs to Locke, Naafiri, Riven, and Sylas, and cheaper crit/lethality items. It also launches the League Classic game mode and delivers sweeping augment and balance-modifier overhauls in ARAM: Mayhem and Arena.
summary: Bel'Veth is functionally a new champion — Q, W, E, and R all rebuilt, with W now pure AP and Q gated by a long per-lane cooldown.
Locke, Naafiri, Riven, and Sylas all take nerfs to their damage and scaling.
Yun Tal Wildarrows is cheaper with more attack speed, and Bastionbreaker dropped 200g while hitting harder.
Jack of All Trades gives less adaptive force at both stat breakpoints.
changelogHighlights: New game mode: League Classic — 60 champions playing their 2010s-era kits.
Ranked Season 3 began July 29; Aegis of Valor no longer reduces LP loss and now grants double LP on wins.
Arena and ARAM: Mayhem augment pools changed — Arena removes Slow and Steady and adds a level-2 Ok Boomerang, while ARAM adds Chain Reaction and makes Pat on the Back multi-pickable.
Bel'Veth has been reworked from the ground up.

champions.summary: Complete kit rework across base stats and all five abilities.
champions.details: Her base attack speed dropped from 0.85 to 0.67 (with a 100% attack damage modifier), Void Surge now has a 4-second-down-to-1-second per-direction cooldown at a flat 850 speed and no longer gets a minion damage modifier, Above And Below became a pure 150% AP scaling ability, Royal Maelstrom's damage reduction and lifesteal now scale by rank, and Endless Banquet applies its passive on every attack with much stronger heal scaling — if you played her on autopilot this patch, your muscle memory is actively costing you games.
champions.name: Bel'Veth

champions.summary: Lower health plus big cuts to Q damage and W move speed and grey health.
champions.details: Base health fell 655 to 620, Ritual Nails lost 10 damage per nail (30 on a full three-nail hit), and Soul Ignition is locked to a flat 40% move speed with reduced grey health scaling, so his snowball and escape pressure are both noticeably weaker in skirmishes.
champions.name: Locke

champions.summary: The Call of the Pack damage cut and moved to bonus AD scaling.
champions.details: Her ultimate's base damage dropped from 150/225/300 to 125/200/275 and both the base and per-packmate ratios now scale off bonus AD instead of total AD, so early-ult all-ins and lane skirmishes hit meaningfully softer before you finish items.
champions.name: Naafiri

champions.summary: Blade of the Exile and Wind Slash both scale worse with bonus AD.
champions.details: Her ultimate's bonus AD ratio fell from 25% to 20% and Wind Slash scales 55%-165% instead of 60%-180%, which directly shaves damage off the execute you rely on to close out duels.
champions.name: Riven

champions.summary: Chain Lash first-lash damage and AP ratio reduced.
champions.details: First lash now deals 40/60/80/100/120 (+40% AP) instead of up to 140 (+45% AP), weakening his poke-heavy laning phase where the first hit does most of his early trading work.
champions.name: Sylas

champions.summary: Death's Grasp cooldown lowered but Realm of Death steals fewer stats.
champions.details: E is 2 seconds shorter on cooldown at every rank while his ultimate now steals 10% of stats instead of 13%, so he pulls more often in teamfights but wins 1v1 death realms by a smaller margin.
champions.name: Mordekaiser

champions.summary: Caustic Wounds passive damage increased at max level and per stack.
champions.details: Second Skin now scales to 30 base (from 24) and 8 per stack (from 6), giving her a bit more chip damage in extended fights where she stacks plasma repeatedly.
champions.name: Kai'Sa

champions.summary: Bramble Smash hits monsters harder and scales better with AP.
champions.details: Q's monster damage modifier went up by 10 at every rank and its AP ratio rose from 40% to 50%, speeding up jungle clear and improving his scaling as a damage-oriented tank.
champions.name: Maokai

champions.summary: More armor growth and a shorter Elastic Slingshot cooldown.
champions.details: Armor growth rose 4.7 to 5.2 and E is 1 second shorter at every rank, meaning more frequent engage attempts and better durability as the game goes long.
champions.name: Zac

champions.summary: Thundering Smash cooldown reduced at early ranks.
champions.details: Q drops from 14 seconds to 12 at rank 1, letting him chase and re-engage more often in the early skirmishes that define his tempo.
champions.name: Volibear

champions.summary: Base move speed increased from 330 to 335.
champions.details: A small mobility bump that makes his headbutt-pulverize combo slightly easier to land in lane and roams marginally faster.
champions.name: Alistar

items.details: Now 750g at 45% attack speed, making it a stronger and faster crit component — if you're an ADC still skipping it, that's a build-order problem.
items.name: Yun Tal Wildarrows

items.summary: 200g cheaper and Shaped Charge deals 20 more true damage.
items.details: Costs 3000g with Shaped Charge at 50 (+150% lethality) true damage, making it a much better-value lethality pickup for divers and bruisers going through frontline HP.
items.name: Bastionbreaker

items.summary: Shadow on-hit now scales with AD and AP.
items.details: The 30 magic damage on-hit now adds 10% bonus AD and 10% AP, so it keeps paying off deeper into the game on on-hit carries instead of falling off.
items.name: Terminus

systems.summary: Jack of All Trades grants less adaptive force at both breakpoints.
systems.details: The 5- and 10-stat rewards fell from 10/25 to 8/20 adaptive force, slightly weakening the greedy stat-stacking builds that lean on it.

systems.summary: Ranked Season 3 began July 29 with reworked Aegis of Valor and apex duo limits.
systems.details: Aegis of Valor no longer softens LP losses and instead grants double LP on wins with no minimum mastery score, while Master can only duo with nearby ranks and GM/Challenger (or GM/Challenger MMR) players can't duo at all — so losses hurt full price now.

systems.summary: League Classic launches with 60 champions on their 2010s-era kits.
systems.details: A throwback mode built around old-school gameplay and graphics that emphasizes strategy over mechanics, with a restricted 60-champion roster.

systems.summary: Damage modifiers now cover item and Augment damage, plus a wide augment rebalance.
systems.details: Champion damage-dealt modifiers apply to spell, attack, item, and Augment damage instead of only spells and attacks, dozens of champions were normalized toward 100%, and augments shifted heavily — Titan's Resolve and Earthwake got stronger, Critical Missile and Drop Bear's stun got cut, Chain Reaction is new, and Pat on the Back can now be taken by multiple players.

systems.summary: Augment level caps cut to 2, crit converts 1:1 to adaptive force, and many champions retuned.
systems.details: Demonic Clasp, Critical Rhythm, Laser Eyes, Spellwake, Earthwake, and Tap Dancer now cap at level 2 with rebalanced values, Slow and Steady was removed, Ok Boomerang gained a second boomerang at level 2, crit-to-adaptive-force conversion improved from 0.68:1 to 1:1, and Thresh, Twisted Fate, Warwick, Nocturne, and Kai'Sa got sizeable buffs while Seraphine's Q was cut.
